transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I'm here because I've been losing a lot of weight recently and my family was getting worried. Honestly, I've just been eating very little lately, sometimes only a bite or two a day.
I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch what you said. What would you like to know more about?
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, and then try to get rid of it by vomiting, laxatives, or other means?
No, I don't do anything like that at all. I never binge eat or make myself throw up, and I don't use laxatives. Instead, I just try to restrict my food intake and eat as little as possible.
Have you been feeling sad, empty, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, over the past few weeks?
No, I haven't really been feeling sad or hopeless lately. I'm mostly just anxious about my weight and making sure I don't eat too much.
Do you have a fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even though you're already underweight?
Yes, I am absolutely terrified of gaining weight or becoming fat. Even though everyone says I'm underweight, I still feel like I need to lose more weight and cannot let my weight go up at all.
Do you think your weight or body shape has a significant impact on your self-worth, and is it a major part of how you evaluate yourself as a person?
I'm not really sure about that, and I haven't really thought about my self-worth in that way. I'm mostly just focused on keeping my weight down and making sure I don't gain any fat.
When you think about what makes you a good or worthy person, do you think your weight or appearance plays a role in that, even if it's not the only thing you consider?

Yes, honestly, my weight and appearance play a huge role in how I view myself. If I gain even a little bit of weight, I feel like an absolute failure and lose all my confidence. Staying thin is really the only thing that makes me feel okay and in control of my life.

The patient's anxiety about weight and appearance, as well as their self-worth being heavily influenced by their weight, further supports the diagnosis of Anorexia Nervosa.
